setup.description: Step-by-step instructions for access control, enterprise SSO, MCP, Microsoft integrations, monitoring, and secure backup and restore operations.

access.modelTitle: The permission model in four building blocks
access.modelDescription: Roles, groups, knowledge spaces, and ACLs serve different purposes. Their combination determines effective access.
access.roleText: A role globally defines which actions a user may perform in principle, such as reading the wiki, updating pages, or managing groups.
access.groupText: A group bundles users such as IT, HR, or Management so permissions do not need to be maintained for every individual.
access.spaceText: A knowledge space combines related wiki content, shared notes, and standards under one navigation and security root.
access.aclText: A resource ACL allows or denies a concrete action for a group or user on a space, category, folder, or entry.
access.formula: Effective access = global role/user permission AND a matching space/resource rule. An ACL can never add a globally missing permission.
access.workflowDescription: This order keeps global capabilities and domain-specific access boundaries clearly separated.

1.title: Define the role
1.text: Under Roles & permissions, define what a user may do in principle. An editor might read and update pages but not manage users.

2.title: Group users
2.text: Create domain-specific user groups and add the appropriate people as members. If needed, appoint a manager for that group only.

3.title: Create a knowledge space
3.text: Create a space, enable the required content types, and select Restricted if only explicitly allowed users should be able to discover it.

4.title: Grant the base rule
4.text: Allow the intended group to read and, if required, update the knowledge space. Enable inheritance so the rule applies to content below it.

5.title: Refine exceptions
5.text: Add more specific rules to categories, folders, or individual entries, such as a read denial for a particularly confidential page.

6.title: Evaluate effective access
6.text: Select a user in the permissions dialog and verify the decision, source, inheritance path, and reason before using the space in production.

access.spaceSettingsDescription: Space settings describe the container. Actual user and group decisions are made through the permissions dialog.

visibility.title: Visibility
visibility.text: Open means the global role permission is normally sufficient unless a specific ACL contradicts it. Restricted additionally requires a matching ALLOW rule.

kinds.title: Enabled content types
kinds.text: Determines whether the space may contain wiki content, shared notes, and/or standards. This is a structural setting, not a user permission.

responsible.title: Responsible group
responsible.text: Documents the business owner of the space. This assignment intentionally grants no access.

rules.title: Manage permissions
rules.text: Opens ACL management for direct rules, inheritance, inheritance boundaries, and effective access preview.

access.responsibilityWarning: “Responsible group: IT” alone does not make the space private and does not grant the IT group access. Use Restricted visibility and an ACL rule for the IT group.
access.ruleDescription: Each rule combines recipient, action, decision, and reach. The location of the rule determines its level in the hierarchy.
access.inheritanceValue: This target only or all children
access.prioritySpecific: The most specific rule wins: entry before folder, folder before category, category before knowledge space.
access.priorityUser: At the same target, a direct user rule wins over group rules.
access.priorityDeny: For conflicting group rules at the same target, DENY wins.
access.priorityGlobal: Global role permissions, individual user denials, and API-key limits always remain the upper bound.
access.managerDescription: A local group manager and global member management are deliberately separate powers and must not be confused.
access.localManagerText: The manager role is assigned to a user inside exactly one group and is the recommended delegation for a domain group owner.
access.localManagerAdd: May search for and add regular members to their own group.
access.localManagerRemove: May remove regular members from their own group.
access.localManagerLimits: Cannot appoint or remove managers, rename or delete groups, or manage other groups.
access.globalManagerText: This role permission is a global administrative capability intended for central administrators, not ordinary group managers.
access.globalManagerAll: May manage memberships in every group.
access.globalManagerRoles: May change membership roles between MEMBER and MANAGER.
access.globalManagerUse: Should be granted together with groups:read only to central group administrators.
access.managerWarning: For an IT group manager, assign the MANAGER membership role inside the IT group. Do not also grant groups:manage_members unless they should manage other groups.
access.exampleDescription: Ali should work as an editor only in the restricted “IT internal” space.
access.exampleRoleText: Ali globally has pages:read and pages:update, so he may read and update wiki content in principle.
access.exampleGroupText: Ali is a MEMBER of the IT group. Another user may be a MANAGER who maintains only this group's memberships.
access.exampleSpaceText: The space is restricted. The IT group receives inheritable ALLOW rules for reading and updating.
access.exampleResult: Ali can use his editor capabilities in IT internal. Without an allow rule, he cannot discover other restricted spaces. A globally missing delete permission remains denied despite the ACL.
access.liveDescription: Changes to role permissions, group memberships, spaces, and resource ACLs are signaled to signed-in clients.
access.liveSocketText: Navigation, dashboard, wiki, notes, standards, search, graph, media, and administration lists reload their visible data after an access change.
access.previewText: The preview uses the same backend decision service as REST, search, exports, MCP, and integrations and explains the deciding rule.

identity.modelDescription: Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak, and other OIDC providers confirm identity. AD-Wiki roles, groups, knowledge spaces, and ACLs remain the sole source of authorization.
identity.authenticationText: The provider checks password, MFA, and account status and supplies a signed OIDC token.
identity.mappingText: Stable external group IDs, full Keycloak paths, or app roles are explicitly mapped to local groups and roles.
identity.authorizationText: Only the existing AD-Wiki permissions and resource ACLs allow an action on a space or content item.
identity.emergencyHint: The protected local emergency account remains available independently of the provider. External claims can neither alter nor replace it.
identity.entraDescription: Follow this order from the Entra app to the first secure sign-in. Tenant ID, client ID, and provider slug are three different values.

1.title: Register the Entra app
1.text: Open Microsoft Entra admin center → Identity → Applications → App registrations → New registration. Select accounts in this organizational directory only. Record the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID.

2.title: Create the client secret
2.text: Open Certificates & secrets → New client secret. Immediately copy the secret value, not the secret ID. The value is shown once and is stored encrypted by AD-Wiki.

3.title: Create an inactive provider in AD-Wiki
3.text: Select Microsoft Entra ID. Enter the display name, tenant ID, client ID, and secret value. Leave the discovery URL empty. The openid profile email scopes are enough for normal sign-in; User.Read is only needed for Graph fallback.

4.title: Decide how accounts are created
4.text: Enable JIT only when new Entra users should automatically become AD-Wiki users. A normal non-administrative default role is then required. Existing local accounts are never merged by matching email.

5.title: Choose claims
5.text: The default profile claims are sub, email, preferred_username, and name. Entra normally omits email_verified; AD-Wiki handles this specific omission compatibly. Map groups by stable object ID and app roles through the roles claim.

6.title: Save and read the provider slug
6.text: After the first save, AD-Wiki creates a stable provider slug from the display name, for example microsoft-company-account. The slug is only the provider's technical URL name and is unrelated to the tenant ID.

7.title: Register the exact callback in Entra
7.text: Copy the callback URL shown in the provider overview. In Entra, open Authentication → Add a platform → Web and enter this exact redirect URI. Do not use a wildcard or replace the slug with the tenant ID.

8.title: Test, then activate
8.text: Run Test connection first. When discovery, issuer, endpoints, PKCE, and JWKS succeed, enable the provider on the sign-in page. Then test with an intended Entra user while keeping the local emergency account available.

identity.entraClientIdValue: Application ID from the Entra app
identity.slugExplanation: Tenant ID = your Microsoft directory. Client ID = your app registration. Provider slug = the automatically generated AD-Wiki URL name. Only the slug appears in the callback URL.
identity.jitWarning: “Automatic account creation is incomplete” means JIT is enabled without a safe default role. Select a reader or editor role without administrative permissions. If the user already exists locally, sign in locally and link Entra under Profile → Linked sign-ins.
identity.entraOverageWarning: If groups are missing and Entra signals hasgroups or _claim_names.groups, AD-Wiki must never continue with an incomplete authorization decision. Sign-in is rejected clearly unless the enabled Graph fallback succeeds.
identity.keycloakDescription: AD-Wiki continues to use the same generic OIDC code flow. For local LDAP or Active Directory, Keycloak acts as the upstream identity provider.

1.title: Create realm and client
1.text: Create a realm and an OIDC client for AD-Wiki. Use the realm issuer, a confidential client, Authorization Code Flow, and a dedicated client secret.

2.title: Secure the redirect
2.text: Register only the exact AD-Wiki callback as a valid redirect URI. Avoid wildcards for redirects and web origins.

3.title: Add the group mapper
3.text: Add a Group Membership protocol mapper, use groups as the token claim name, and enable full group paths if identically named subgroups can exist.

4.title: Connect LDAP/AD in Keycloak
4.text: Configure LDAP or Active Directory only under User Federation in Keycloak and add its Group Mapper there. Test synchronization and claims in Keycloak before activating AD-Wiki.

identity.keycloakLdapHint: AD-Wiki receives only standardized OIDC claims and stores no LDAP bind DN, passwords, or other AD credentials. Those remain exclusively in Keycloak.
identity.genericTitle: Authentik, Okta, Zitadel, and other OIDC providers
identity.genericDescription: Any standards-compliant provider can use the same flow when discovery, signed ID tokens, and PKCE S256 are available.
identity.genericDiscovery: Use the exact tenant-specific issuer and its OpenID discovery document.
identity.genericClaims: Map sub, email, email_verified, preferred_username, and name; never link existing accounts by matching email alone.
identity.genericRedirect: Register only the provider's exact callback and no freely selectable return targets.
identity.genericPkce: Enable Authorization Code Flow and PKCE S256. Implicit Flow and unsigned tokens are not accepted.
identity.testDescription: The protected connection test reads public metadata and keys only. It does not sign in a user or transmit the client secret.
identity.testDiscoveryText: Loads metadata and compares the published issuer exactly.
identity.testTlsText: Uses the system trust store; internal CAs must be explicitly trusted by the API container.
identity.testJwksText: Retrieves public signing keys and confirms PKCE S256.
identity.testEndpointsText: Reports authorization, token, and optional end-session, frontchannel, and backchannel capabilities.
identity.secretHint: Client secrets and provider tokens never appear in test results, logs, or browser responses. Full provider administration and the UI action for this test follow in phase 15F.

mcp.endpointDescription: The MCP server is a Streamable HTTP endpoint. The displayed URL is derived from this installation's configured API address.
mcp.clientsDescription: OAuth is preferred for interactive clients. A personal bearer token is available for clients without OAuth support.
mcp.codexOauthText: Register the server without --oauth-resource: Codex obtains the resource automatically from server discovery. Then start browser authentication and approve the requested access.
mcp.writeScopeHint: mcp:read is sufficient for read-only access. Add mcp:write only when Codex should create or edit drafts.
mcp.codexTokenText: Create a personal token under MCP access and pass it exclusively through an environment variable. Set the variable in the same PowerShell session before starting Codex.
mcp.tokenWarning: The token inherits your effective user permissions and is not automatically read-only. Never store it directly in config.toml or source code.
mcp.claudeCodeText: Add the HTTP server and check its status first. “Needs authentication” means TLS and MCP are working; then open /mcp and select Authenticate.
mcp.claudeCodeTlsHint: “Failed to connect” before authentication usually indicates missing TLS trust. For a self-signed or internal certificate, trust the issuing CA or the specific certificate locally. Do not disable TLS verification permanently.
mcp.claudeDesktopText: A remote connector is called from the Anthropic cloud, so the server must be publicly reachable.
mcp.claudeDesktopPublic: A publicly resolvable DNS name and reachable HTTPS endpoint.
mcp.claudeDesktopTls: A complete, publicly trusted TLS certificate chain; an internal PKI is normally insufficient for the cloud connector.
mcp.claudeDesktopLocal: localhost and .local addresses only work with local clients such as Codex or Claude Code.
mcp.securityDescription: MCP bypasses neither ACLs nor ownership. “All content” always means only content the authenticated user is allowed to see.
mcp.aclText: Every tool call is evaluated in the authenticated user's context through the central KnowledgeAccessService.
mcp.visibilityText: Content must be enabled for MCP. Private, non-enabled, or archived content is not silently included.
mcp.tokenText: Only the hash is stored. The secret is shown once and can be revoked at any time or given an expiration date.
mcp.draftsText: New pages and standards are created as non-visible drafts. Approval, activation, and permanent deletion are not exposed as MCP tools.
mcp.roleRead: Use the server and view personal tokens
mcp.roleCreate: Create tokens and start OAuth approval
mcp.toolsDescription: Actual execution requires the listed domain permission in addition to mcp:read. Write tools also require the mcp:write OAuth scope or a personal token with the matching user permissions.

toolDescriptions.list_knowledge: Lists enabled knowledge types for which the user has the corresponding read permission; unauthorized types are skipped and each group has its own cursor.
toolDescriptions.search_knowledge: Searches the requested visible and MCP-enabled knowledge types for which the user has the corresponding read permission.
toolDescriptions.list_pages: Lists published wiki pages enabled for MCP, with filtering and pagination.
toolDescriptions.read_page: Reads a visible wiki page by ID or slug.
toolDescriptions.search_notes: Searches owned or shared, non-archived notes enabled for MCP.
toolDescriptions.read_note: Reads an accessible note by ID.
toolDescriptions.list_active_standards: Lists active, currently valid standards enabled for MCP.
toolDescriptions.search_standards: Searches active, currently valid standards enabled for MCP.
toolDescriptions.read_standard: Reads an accessible active standard by ID or slug.
toolDescriptions.evaluate_against_standards: Evaluates supplied structured actual values against active standards and reports deviations.
toolDescriptions.detect_source_conflicts: Detects deterministically verifiable contradictions between structured rules of visible active standards.
toolDescriptions.classify_content: Classifies content as a wiki page, note, or standard.
toolDescriptions.suggest_tags: Suggests existing tags using visible comparison content of the selected knowledge type.
toolDescriptions.suggest_category: Suggests a suitable visible category; read access to the knowledge type adds visible comparison content.
toolDescriptions.create_page: Creates a new wiki page as a draft that is not enabled for MCP.
toolDescriptions.update_page: Updates an existing page draft with version checking.
toolDescriptions.create_note: Creates a private note owned by the authenticated user.
toolDescriptions.update_note: Updates an owned note or a shared note with edit access.
toolDescriptions.create_standard_draft: Creates a non-enabled standard draft; activation remains a manual process.

mcp.resourcesDescription: Clients with resource support can address enabled content directly using these URI templates.
mcp.troubleshootingDescription: The most common causes are OAuth discovery, certificate trust, or a server that has not been restarted after an update.
mcp.troubleshootingAuth: “No authorization support detected”: verify TLS trust and both OAuth metadata endpoints; they must be reachable without a certificate warning.
mcp.troubleshootingTls: Internal PKI: trust root and intermediate certificates on the local computer. Use a publicly trusted certificate for Claude remote connectors.
mcp.troubleshootingTools: Missing tools: rebuild and restart the API after an update, then refresh the tool list or reopen the connection in the client.

integrations.entraDescription: The integration uses the authorization code flow for a personal Microsoft account. The app registration is central, while authentication and stored tokens remain user-specific.

1.title: Create an app registration
1.text: In Microsoft Entra ID, create a new registration under App registrations for the desired account types.

2.title: Configure the Web platform
2.text: Under Authentication, select the Web platform and enter the exact matching redirect URI.

3.title: Add the Graph permission
3.text: Under API permissions > Microsoft Graph > Delegated permissions, add Tasks.ReadWrite.

4.title: Create a client secret
4.text: Create a secret under Certificates & secrets and immediately save its Value, not the Secret ID.

integrations.redirectDescription: Enter one Web redirect URI per environment. Scheme, host, port, and path must exactly match MICROSOFT_REDIRECT_URI.
integrations.redirectWarning: Replace wiki.example.com with your real domain. A different host, missing https, another port, or an extra slash typically results in AADSTS50011.
integrations.graphTitle: Microsoft Graph permissions and OpenID scopes
integrations.graphDescription: Use Delegated permissions, not Application permissions – the integration always acts on behalf of the signed-in user.
integrations.graphSummary: In short: you add exactly one permission in Entra – Tasks.ReadWrite (Delegated). MSAL requests the three OpenID scopes automatically at sign-in, so no manual entry is needed for them in Entra.
integrations.tasksPermission: The only permission you add manually under API permissions. Allows reading and writing the signed-in user's Microsoft To Do lists and tasks.
integrations.openidScopes: No manual entry needed: MSAL requests these scopes itself at sign-in. offline_access allows the connection to be refreshed without another interactive sign-in.
integrations.consentHint: Whether administrator consent is required depends on the Entra tenant's consent policies.
integrations.environmentDescription: The public client configuration and secrets must be set in the backend. In Docker, the two secrets are passed through the AD_WIKI_ variables.
integrations.secretText: MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET or AD_WIKI_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET contains the secret Value. The Secret ID shown in Entra does not work.
integrations.encryptionText: The key must contain exactly 32 random bytes encoded as Base64 and remain stable across restarts. Changing it makes stored OAuth tokens unreadable.
integrations.rightsDescription: These role permissions control which integration actions a user may perform. They are independent from the Microsoft Graph permission.

rights.read: View connection status, available To Do lists, and synchronization history.
rights.create: Start Microsoft OAuth authentication and connect an account.
rights.update: Select lists, synchronize, and create Microsoft tasks from notes.
rights.delete: Disconnect the account and remove the local OAuth token cache.

integrations.workflowDescription: After backend configuration, authorization always takes place in the individual user's account.

workflow.1: Restart the backend and select “Connect Microsoft” under Settings > Integrations.
workflow.2: Sign in to Microsoft and approve Tasks.ReadWrite.
workflow.3: Select the desired To Do lists and save the selection.
workflow.4: Run “Synchronize now” and review the synchronization history.

integrations.troubleshootingDescription: Check the configuration and redirect URI before repeatedly reconnecting a user account.
integrations.errorRedirect: AADSTS50011: compare the Entra redirect URI and MICROSOFT_REDIRECT_URI character by character.
integrations.errorConfig: “Not configured”: set tenant ID, client ID, secret, redirect URI, and the 32-byte encryption key completely.
integrations.errorSecret: invalid_client or expired secret: create a new secret Value, apply it, and restart the backend.
integrations.errorRebuild: Docker environment: rebuild images and containers after changes to variables or code.

monitoring.overviewDescription: AD Wiki provides stable health checks, protected Prometheus metrics, and import templates. The existing monitoring platform handles collection, visualization, and alert delivery.
monitoring.appText: Liveness, readiness, application metrics, example rules, a Grafana dashboard, and a Zabbix guide.
monitoring.operatorText: Prometheus/Grafana or Zabbix, alert receivers, escalation paths, retention, and thresholds adjusted to the environment.
monitoring.stackHint: AD Wiki does not start Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, or Zabbix in its own Compose stack. An existing VM or monitoring installation reads AD Wiki externally.
monitoring.endpointsDescription: Replace wiki.example.com with the externally reachable host name of the installation. Liveness and readiness are suitable for simple HTTP checks; the metrics endpoint provides detailed signals.
monitoring.tokenDescription: AD_WIKI_MONITORING_TOKEN protects only the Prometheus endpoint. Generate the value once at random and store it as a secret in both AD Wiki and the external monitoring platform.
monitoring.tokenWarning: Do not put the token in Git, screenshots, tickets, or a regular configuration file. When rotating it, update AD Wiki and the external scraper together.
monitoring.platformDescription: Choose the path used by the existing operations environment. The examples do not install or start additional services.
monitoring.prometheusText: Prometheus scrapes the metrics with a bearer token. Then load the provided alert rules and import the JSON dashboard into the existing Grafana instance.
monitoring.zabbixText: An HTTP agent item reads the Prometheus text with an Authorization header. Dependent items use Prometheus preprocessing; actions and media remain in Zabbix.
monitoring.packageHint: The files are templates. Adjust target names, data source UIDs, receivers, and thresholds in the existing monitoring platform.
monitoring.metricsDescription: These groups cover the central application states. VM, Docker, PostgreSQL, and Redis system metrics still come from agents or exporters in the external platform.

availability.title: Availability and API
availability.text: Process uptime and PostgreSQL and Redis availability.

backups.title: Backups and workers
backups.text: Stale or failed backups, worker outages, and overdue plans.

capacity.title: Uploads and capacity
capacity.text: Free upload storage and growth of stored media.

security.title: Security and interfaces
security.text: Login, HTTP, API key, and MCP failures without personal labels.

services.title: SMTP, audit, and TLS
services.text: Delivery and audit results plus the lifetime of the certificate readable by the API.

monitoring.thresholdsDescription: The templates contain conservative starting values. Persistent load, latency, and capacity thresholds require a baseline from the real installation.
monitoring.thresholdHint: These values are not immutable product requirements. Operators compare them against RPO, maintenance windows, normal load, and available storage and document any changes.
monitoring.tlsDescription: For a certificate issued by an internal PKI, the external probe must trust the issuing root and, if applicable, intermediate CA. The certificate actually delivered over HTTPS is what matters.
monitoring.tlsHint: Mount the CA chain read-only in the probe and verify the expected server name. Keep insecure_skip_verify false, otherwise a wrong host name or invalid chain would go unnoticed.
monitoring.acceptanceDescription: A monitoring connection is only complete after both measurements and alert delivery have been tested in practice.

acceptance.1: Import the appropriate Prometheus/Grafana files or implement the Zabbix guide.
acceptance.2: Verify liveness, readiness, and metric scraping successfully from the monitoring VM.
acceptance.3: Configure the alert receiver and escalation path in the external platform.
acceptance.4: Trigger test alerts for API outage, worker outage, stale backup, low storage, and certificate expiry through to the receiver.
acceptance.5: Document thresholds, owners, retention, and the acceptance result in the operations runbook.

backups.overviewDescription: AD Wiki backs up the database and uploads as one versioned artifact. Scheduling, workers, retention, remote destinations, and restore preparation are managed centrally in the administration area.
backups.scopeWarning: Redis, TLS certificates, and production secrets are not part of the backup. Store the secrets in a separate password or secret manager.
backups.foundationDescription: Define the host paths for local and optional network backups, the unprivileged container identity, and a persistent 32-byte key before creating the first destination.
backups.keyWarning: The backup key must remain unchanged across restarts and reinstallations. If it is lost, encrypted credentials for remote destinations can no longer be decrypted.
backups.foundationMount: BACKUP_LOCAL_PATH points to local host storage. BACKUP_NETWORK_PATH optionally points to an SMB, NFS, or other network path already mounted by the host operating system. AD Wiki does not mount shares itself.
backups.foundationWorker: The backup worker runs unprivileged, without a Docker socket, and with read-only upload access. BACKUP_UID and BACKUP_GID need write access to the configured host paths.
backups.foundationSecrets: The PostgreSQL password and backup key are mounted as Docker secrets. Never place secret values in the Compose file or Git repository.
backups.destinationsDescription: Local and mounted storage always follows the same sequence: prepare the path on the host, rebuild the containers, then select the preconfigured mount in backup management.
backups.mountStepHostText: Create local storage or mount an SMB/NFS share through the Docker host operating system. The path must remain available and be writable by BACKUP_UID/BACKUP_GID. On Windows, use forward slashes, for example D:/Backups.
backups.mountStepContainerText: Set BACKUP_LOCAL_PATH or BACKUP_NETWORK_PATH in .env.production, then rebuild the containers so the worker can access the path.
backups.mountStepUiText: Under Settings > Backups choose Preconfigured mount, select Local or Network mount as the storage location, and optionally set a subdirectory.
backups.destinationSftpText: Use a dedicated SSH key, a restricted destination account, and mandatory host-key fingerprint verification.
backups.destinationS3Text: Preferred offsite destination with HTTPS, dedicated bucket permissions, an optional prefix, and server-side encryption.
backups.destinationMountText: Uses either BACKUP_LOCAL_PATH or BACKUP_NETWORK_PATH. A local path is fast; a network mount can provide a separate copy.
backups.destinationTestText: Checks write, read, delete, and checksum as an asynchronous job, plus authentication for SFTP and S3. Credentials remain redacted from the API, logs, and audit entries.
backups.offsiteRecommendation: Maintain at least two copies on separate systems, with at least one encrypted copy outside the Docker host.
backups.scheduleDescription: Schedules use a time, IANA time zone, and weekdays instead of free-form cron expressions. Redis locks prevent duplicate runs after restarts or with multiple API instances.
backups.scheduleDestinationText: Select the destination type and save its configuration. Test the destination; SFTP and S3 must pass the connection test before production use.
backups.schedulePlanText: Set a name, destination, local time, time zone, weekdays, and daily, weekly, and monthly retention. The next run is shown immediately.
backups.scheduleVerifyText: Start a backup with “Run now”. Check status, duration, size, checksum, and job history, then test an administrator notification.
backups.scheduleHint: During the consistent snapshot, new write operations briefly receive HTTP 503 while reads remain available. The barrier is also released automatically after an error.
backups.restoreDescription: The web interface checks availability, integrity, compatibility, required secrets, and free space. The destructive restore itself intentionally runs only in the isolated operations container.
backups.restorePrepareText: Select an available restore point in the restore assistant and start the preflight. Then open the verified six-step runbook or download it as Markdown.
backups.restoreStopText: Announce the maintenance window and stop all publicly reachable and writing services. PostgreSQL remains available to the operations container.
backups.restoreDryRunText: The dry run verifies the manifest, SHA-256 checksums, paths, PostgreSQL dump, and upload archive without changing production data.
backups.restoreExecuteText: Confirm the real run with the backup ID shown in the manifest. The database and uploads are replaced, then Prisma migrations are applied.
backups.restoreStartTitle: Start services in a controlled way
backups.restoreStartText: Start the API, worker, web app, and reverse proxy again. Wait until every container reports healthy; inspect API and operations logs first if a service fails.
backups.restoreValidateText: Verify administrator login, roles and ACLs, wiki pages, notes, standards, media, and download paths. Record the result, duration, RPO/RTO, and any anomalies in the restore log.
backups.restoreWarning: A restore overwrites the current database and uploads. Never run it against an actively used environment, and always verify the dry run, backup ID, and maintenance window first.
backups.rightsDescription: Backup permissions are separated so monitoring, configuration, execution, and restore preparation can follow the principle of least privilege.

rights.read: View destinations, plans, backups, integrity status, and job history.
rights.create: Create storage destinations and backup plans.
rights.update: Edit destinations, schedules, retention, and activation, and run connection tests.
rights.delete: Remove obsolete destinations and plans; protected or referenced destinations are rejected.
rights.run: Start a backup manually with “Run now”.
rights.restore: Check restore compatibility, download backups, and use the guided restore preparation.

backups.monitoringDescription: Dashboards and alerts must monitor not only failures but, most importantly, the age of the last successful backup.
backups.monitoringFreshness: Alert when there is no successful backup within the defined RPO window.
backups.monitoringFailure: Notify administrators about failures, authentication issues, and unexpectedly long or concurrent jobs.
backups.monitoringCapacity: Monitor size, duration, and free space so gradual growth is detected early.
backups.monitoringDrill: Run a monthly integrity check and regularly perform a full restore in an isolated test environment.
backups.troubleshootingDescription: Use the error code in job history and check destination, capacity, and integrity first. Never copy secrets into tickets or logs for troubleshooting.
backups.errorDestination: Destination unreachable or authentication failed: check DNS, routing, TLS or host key, destination account, and the connection test.
backups.errorSpace: Out of space: check free capacity on local and remote destinations, then review retention. Never manually mark incomplete artifacts as valid.
backups.errorIntegrity: Checksum or manifest failure: quarantine the backup and do not restore it. Create a new backup and inspect the storage medium or transfer path.
backups.errorBarrier: Write barrier does not expire: inspect active write operations and Redis. The worker releases the barrier after failure; only retry after that.
backups.errorKey: Key lost or changed: do not overwrite existing encrypted destination configurations with a new key. Restore the secured original key or recreate destinations with new credentials.
